subject: Legacy marketplace credits applied to multiple entities — evidence & reclaim plan
body:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cloudreseller.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 Sep 2028 08:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Legacy credits applied across resold entities — initial data

Hi Diego,

Thanks for flagging this. We pulled the allocation report for July–August and there are indeed several legacy credit allocations that were attached to the reseller ledger before the entity split. I attached a CSV extract with invoice line items (CR-Invoice-202806-alloc.csv) and a short audit PDF that shows the credit application timestamps.

A few quick notes from our side:
- The credits were created on 2028-06-28 as a bulk adjustment tied to our global contract.
- They were posted to the top-level reseller ledger and then mapped to downstream accounts by a nightly job; that job did not consider the new VAT entity field introduced on 2028-07-01.
- We can produce transaction IDs and the raw usage lines, but we will need Redwood to confirm which legal entities should have retained vs reclaimed those credits so we can push corrective invoices.

Let us know the target entity split and any tax team contacts if VAT reallocation is required.

Best,
Elena
Account Lead — CloudReseller Inc

-----Original Message-----
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Sent: Fri, 08 Sep 2028 17:03:00 +0000
To: elena.rossi@cloudreseller.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com; priyom_das@redwood.com
Subject: Legacy credits applied across resold entities — noticed on GCP ledger

Elena —

We spotted negative adjustments on our consolidated marketplace invoice for June that look like credits were applied against the reseller account rather than split by the new EU/UK entities. The billing team needs:

1) A map of marketplace transaction IDs to Redwood customer entity IDs for all credit lines in June/July.
2) Original invoices where credits were first posted.
3) Confirmation of VAT treatment the reseller used when creating the bulk credit.

Kimberly/ Priyom — looping you in because this will impact reclaiming flows and VAT evidence we need to send finance.

Diego
Director, Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

---

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: elena.rossi@cloudreseller.com
Date: Tue, 11 Sep 2028 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Legacy credits applied across resold entities — initial data

Thanks Elena — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from finance/compliance:

- We need the credit creation journal entries (not just invoice extracts). The CSV gives us line items, but the VAT reconciliation needs the journal sequence and the tax rate applied per line.
- Please indicate whether any credit reversal will generate additional downstream invoices (i.e., will end-customers see adjustments or will you net internally?).
- If downstream invoices change, we will need a list of impacted customers (email + entity) so we can coordinate VAT notifications in the EU and UK.

Action items for us: Priyom, can you pull the affected invoice IDs (from our side) and the sample customer notifications so we can mirror the language?

Kimberly Park
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

On Wed, 12 Sep 2028 at 11:22, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com> wrote:

> Diego / Kimberly / Elena —
>
> I pulled the invoice slices from our ledger (attached gcp-legacy-credit-trail.pdf). Quick summary: 47 affected invoices across EU entities, 12 in UK, and 6 in our APAC reseller test accounts (these should be ignored for reclaim).
>
> Questions for CloudReseller:
> - Will you issue corrective invoices to the reseller top-level account or directly to the downstream customers?
> - Do you have the original VAT rates per invoice line? The PDF has line items but not tax codes.
>
> Next steps (internal):
> - Diego: confirm which EU entity should own the credits (EU-Redwood-1 vs EU-Redwood-2) and whether Redwood will absorb any portion.
> - Kimberly: prepare a draft notification for customers if CloudReseller will re-invoice downstream.
>
> Priyom Das
> Revenue Ops Analyst
> Redwood Inference
>
On Thu, 13 Sep 2028 at 16:03, diego_fernandez@redwood.com wrote:

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: elena.rossi@cloudreseller.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 13 Sep 2028 16:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Legacy credits applied across resold entities — initial data

Elena / team —

Thanks for the extracts — confirmed receipt of CSV + PDF. Internal decisions:

- We will instruct CloudReseller to reassign 80% of the legacy credits to EU-Redwood-1 and 20% to EU-Redwood-2. APAC test accounts should be excluded.
- Redwood will not absorb any credit value; we want corrective invoices issued upstream to the reseller and downstream notifications if customer-facing invoices change.
- For VAT, please provide the journal entries and tax rate per invoice line. Our tax counsel (VAT-eu@tax-advisor.com) will review and advise on whether the correction triggers VAT adjustments for the downstream customers.

Action items and deadlines:
- CloudReseller to provide journal entries & transaction IDs by EOD 2028-09-15. (Elena)
- Priyom to prepare impacted customer list and draft notification by 2028-09-14. (Priyom)
- Kimberly to confirm reclaim accounting flow with finance by 2028-09-16. (Kimberly)

Please reply if any of those dates are a hard blocker.

Diego Fernandez
Director, Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: CR-Invoice-202806-alloc.csv (text/csv), gcp-legacy-credit-trail.pdf (application/pdf)]
